name: Alfred Hitchcock
hook: The master of suspense, his landmark films and the details Jeopardy keeps asking about them.

facts.label: the master of suspense
facts.statement: Alfred Hitchcock, the "master of suspense," was born August 13, 1899 — a Friday the 13th whose centennial fell in 1999.

facts.label: Psycho
facts.statement: Psycho (1960) kills off its major star early in the film; Bernard Herrmann scored it for strings only.

facts.label: North by Northwest
facts.statement: North by Northwest (1959) ends with a chase on Mount Rushmore, where James Mason's Vandamm falls.

facts.label: The Birds
facts.statement: The Birds adapts a Daphne du Maurier novelette about gulls turned violent.

facts.label: Vertigo
facts.statement: Vertigo (1958) stars James Stewart as a San Francisco detective paralyzed by a fear of heights.

facts.label: Rear Window
facts.statement: Rear Window came from Cornell Woolrich's story "It Had to Be Murder" and traps Jimmy Stewart in a wheelchair.

facts.label: Rebecca
facts.statement: Rebecca (1940) is the only Hitchcock film to win the Best Picture Oscar.
